reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an educational walkthrough of a Google IT Support course and demonstrates completing a Coursera binary-counting exercise with a visible correct result. The request to subscribe, like, and share is ordinary audience engagement and is not linked to payment, investment, credentials, or another deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: In this video i am going to show you Google IT support fundamentals binaries
This is a small quiz like you are going to solve that is the quiz called How to count in binary. We are going to solve this as well.
My first test success, No error with 1 hundred percent marks

opening.argument: The presentation turns an assessment result into a promotional hook rather than merely explaining binary arithmetic. The host asks viewers to subscribe, like, and share, while emphasizing that the demonstrated task produced “100% marks” and that the course can be completed through online assessments. That pairing encourages engagement around an apparently easy route to a valuable course result, while the video does not establish what viewers would actually receive, whether the result is transferable, or whether completing the demonstrated steps provides the claimed broader benefits. A solicitation built around an attractive outcome but lacking those qualifications warrants treating it as a possible low-barrier acquisition pitch.

citations.quote: please subscribe our channel and like and share
solve the Google IT Support Professional Certificate Course Binary Assignment with 100% marks
My first test success, No error with 1 hundred percent marks

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this ordinary engagement, but that does not answer the central concern: the engagement request appears in a video built around a perfect assessment result and course-related benefits. Showing a completed screen proves only that a screen was shown; it does not establish that viewers can obtain the same result, that the qualification has the advertised value, or that the promoted pathway is reliable. The defense therefore treats promotional framing as neutral without addressing the missing qualifications.

citations.quote: please subscribe our channel and like and share
We now have 100% grade and we have passed

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument never identifies a reward offered to viewers in exchange for subscribing or sharing. The engagement request is generic, while the perfect score belongs to the presenter’s demonstrated assessment. The material describes coursework and an exercise, not a cash, asset, or withdrawal scheme; the argument’s references to an “easy route” and an unverified qualification are interpretations, not shown outcomes.

citations.quote: In this video i am going to show you Google IT support fundamentals binaries
This is a small quiz like you are going to solve that is the quiz called How to count in binary.
My first test success, No error with 1 hundred percent marks

opening.argument: Several signals deserve scrutiny in combination: the description promotes a binary assignment solution with “100% marks,” the narration repeatedly highlights passing, and the description supplies a Coursera link while directing viewers to additional course-solution videos. Those are not proof of fraud individually, but they create a low-friction promise of successful completion and direct viewers toward an external course pathway. The video gives little basis for judging whether the result reflects genuine learning, authorized assistance, or a dependable benefit for viewers. A careful reviewer should therefore treat the confident perfect-result framing and external redirection as scam-like risk signals rather than accepting the educational label at face value.

citations.quote: solve the Google IT Support Professional Certificate Course Binary Assignment with 100% marks
Coursera Link : coursera.org
We now have 100% grade and we have passed

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to a visible result, but a visible result can also be the persuasive centerpiece of a promotion. It does not resolve the external-link and additional-video funnel, nor does it show that the presenter’s method is appropriate for viewers or that the certificate-related claims follow from one quiz. The absence of overt payment language is not evidence that the promotional pathway is trustworthy.

citations.quote: Coursera Link : coursera.org
Video Link : https://youtu.be/1b1y7lF3XvM
We now have 100% grade and we have passed

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited links are course and related-video references, not a claim that viewers must deposit money, surrender credentials, or claim an asset. The perfect grade is shown as the presenter’s result on a binary quiz, and the frames visibly show the exercise and a correct result. Nothing here links a reward to an audience action or establishes deceptive acquisition.

citations.quote: This is a small quiz like you are going to solve that is the quiz called How to count in binary.
ABOUT COURSE : This 5-course certificate, developed by Google

opening.argument: Although presented as instruction, the content functions prominently as promotion for a course and the presenter’s surrounding channel. The description advertises a certificate, says it can prepare viewers for entry-level IT work, lists employers, mentions a dual credential, and points to more solution videos. The narration also asks viewers to subscribe and share. This is more than a neutral explanation of binary notation: it uses a successful assessment demonstration and career-oriented claims to steer viewers toward participation in a broader pathway. The perfect-result emphasis can make that pathway appear unusually accessible, supporting concern that the educational framing masks promotional acquisition.

citations.quote: This 5-course certificate, developed by Google, includes innovative curriculum designed to prepare you for an entry-level role in IT support.
You can also earn a CompTIA and Google dual credential
please subscribe our channel and like and share
My first test success, No error with 1 hundred percent marks

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material educational does not neutralize its promotional elements. The description makes career and credential claims well beyond the binary exercise, while the video directs viewers to further solution content and requests channel engagement. The defense focuses narrowly on the quiz and omits how those broader claims and calls to action frame the demonstration as a participation funnel.

citations.quote: A job in IT can mean in-person or remote help desk work
You can also earn a CompTIA and Google dual credential
please subscribe our channel and like and share

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotional context does not make educational content a scam. The description identifies a real five-course certificate and explains its subject areas, while the video demonstrates a specific binary-counting assessment. Career possibilities and credential information are not a promise that viewers will receive money or an asset for participating, and the argument does not show any deceptive mechanism.
